## Summary

`from_json` is a three-pass pipeline: **parse → decode → validate**, each walking the full input/tree. Depth is the only limit enforced before materialization; every other limit is checked in `Doc::new` after the entire tree, every attribute value, and every run has been allocated. `Doc::validate` then walks the tree a second time and re-does schema/type/URL/content checks already performed during decode. `JsonValue` is a fully owned DOM (`kind` + start offset, no end spans), so there is no zero-copy path; every JSON string is copied at least twice (parse into `Box<str>`, decode into `Box<str>`/`String`, then again on run splitting).

## Files

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `crates/rich-editor-auy/src/wire/parser.rs:26-40` | `from_json`, `check_json` |
| `.../wire/parser.rs:53-102` | `decode_doc`, `decode_blocks`, `check_doc` |
| `.../wire/parser.rs:118-231` | `decode_block` (depth check :125, content classification :186-207, run normalization :214-215, child `Arc` alloc :221-229) |
| `.../wire/parser.rs:233-270` | `decode_inline` (text copy :256, marks :255) |
| `.../wire/attrs.rs:47-111` | `decode_attrs` (object check :55, member loop :63, value copy :71, duplicate/required :97-110) |
| `.../wire/attrs.rs:113-149` | `decode_value` (string copy :115-118, list/map :134-145) |
| `.../wire/attrs.rs:152-202` | `decode_ref` |
| `.../wire/attrs.rs:204-229` | `decode_any` (recursive, uncounted) |
| `.../wire/attrs.rs:231-278` | `decode_marks` (per-mark Vec :252, `Attrs::new` :273, `with_mark` :275) |
| `.../wire/json.rs:9-16` | `JsonValue { kind, start }` |
| `.../wire/json_parser.rs:26-40` | `parse_json` |
| `.../wire/json_parser.rs:52-53,72-79,119-126` | depth checks before descend |
| `.../wire/json_parser.rs:82-117` | object body: Vec of `(Box<str>, JsonValue)` :85/:99, `BTreeSet` dup check :110 |
| `.../wire/json_parser.rs:129-149` | array body: Vec push :138 |
| `.../wire/json_parser.rs:152-184` | unescaped string `Box::from(text)` :170 |
| `.../wire/json_parser.rs:186-...` | escaped string `String` growth |
| `.../wire/json_escape.rs:13-54` | escape decoder |
| `.../wire/options.rs:4-9` | `ParseOptions { limits }` |
| `.../wire/fragment.rs:33-63` | fragment path (`Doc::new` :56, `check_doc` :61) |
| `.../wire/envelope.rs:65-108` | envelope path (`decode_doc`, no separate validate beyond it) |
| `.../wire/view.rs:16-...` | `write_view_into` (projection) |
| `.../model/doc.rs:82-118` | `Doc::new` limits scan |
| `.../model/doc.rs:129-131` | `from_blocks` |
| `.../model/limits.rs:14-46` | per-block/run/text limits |
| `.../model/limits.rs:58-66` | attrs-per-node limit |
| `.../model/limits.rs:76-109` | value recursion/depth |
| `.../model/limits.rs:113-121` | `max_attr_string_bytes` |
| `.../model/validate.rs:46-88` | `Doc::validate` |
| `.../model/validate.rs:96-190` | `validate_block` |
| `.../model/validate.rs:246-...` | `validate_marks` |
| `.../model/text.rs:89-104` | `TextBlock::new` re-push/merge |
| `.../model/text.rs:183-218` | `normalize` splitting + per-chunk String/mark clone |
| `.../model/marks.rs:105-131` | `with_mark` clones whole attr vector per mark |
| `.../model/attrs.rs:100-112` | `Attrs::new` sort/box |
| `crates/rich-editor-auy/src/lib.rs:44-75` | `Limits` definition/defaults |
| `fuzz/fuzz_targets/json_parse.rs`, `a11y_tree.rs`, `apply_step.rs` | fuzz entry points |
| `bench/benches/hot_path.rs:47-98` | parse/serialize benchmarks |

## Architecture

```
from_json ─► parse_json (owned DOM, copies strings, depth-capped)
          ─► decode_doc ─► decode_attrs / decode_blocks ─► decode_block ─► decode_inline
                          │                              └─ TextBlock::new → normalize
                          └─ Doc::new  (whole-tree limit scan)
          ─► check_doc ─► Doc::validate (whole-tree schema/structural scan)
```
`fragment.rs` and `envelope.rs` reuse `decode_doc`/`decode_blocks` + `Doc::new` + `check_doc`. Writers are the inverse (not on this path).

## Report — ordered gap list

### 1. Limits enforced too late (materialization precedes rejection)

| Limit | Enforced at | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| `max_depth` | `json_parser.rs:52,73,120`; `parser.rs:125` | early (only good case) |
| `max_attrs_per_node` | `limits.rs:59-65` via `Doc::new:100` | after all attrs built |
| `max_attr_string_bytes` | `limits.rs:113-121` via `Doc::new` | after every string/list/map built |
| `max_mark_attrs` | `limits.rs:29-39` via `Doc::new` | after mark attrs built |
| `max_runs_per_block` | `limits.rs:17-23` via `Doc::new` | after `TextBlock::new` + `normalize` (normalize can *increase* run count) |
| `max_block_text_bytes` | `limits.rs:24-46` via `Doc::new` | after full text copy/split |
| `max_doc_bytes` / `max_nodes` | `doc.rs:101-117` | after all `Arc<Block>` and runs exist |
| **marks per run** | **nowhere** | missing as a limit; schema caps marks at 64 (`schema/builder.rs:72`), `MarkSet` mask is `u64` (`marks.rs:42`), `bit` drops ids ≥64 (`marks.rs:173-176`) — unreachable today but unbounded per run |

Per-stage allocations on `from_json`:
1. `parse_json`: one `Box<str>` per string/key (`json_parser.rs:170`, escaped path; `:85/:99`), one `Vec`/`Box<[..]>` per array/object (`:85,99,138`), `BTreeSet` per object for dup keys (`:110`).
2. `decode_attrs`: `Vec<Attr>` (`attrs.rs:62,92`), second string copy (`:115-118`, `:208`), `Vec` for list/map (`:134-145`, `:222`), key clone (`:144,:223`); no limits parameter, so a multi-MB attr string is fully allocated before `Doc::new` rejects it.
3. `decode_marks`: `Vec<Attr>` per mark (`:252`), `Attrs::new` sort/box (`:273`), and `with_mark` clones the whole accumulated mark-attr vector per mark → O(k²) allocations (`marks.rs:105-131`).
4. `decode_blocks`/`decode_block`: `Vec<Arc<Block>>` (`parser.rs:96-100,221-229`), one `Arc` per block; `child_kinds` Vec per container (`:189-202`); inline `Vec<InlineItem>` (`:210-213`).
5. `TextBlock::new` re-pushes all items into a new Vec (`text.rs:89-104`); `normalize` allocates a second Vec and one new `String` + mark clone per split (`text.rs:183-218`).
6. `Doc::new` scans everything (`doc.rs:89,100,103`), then `Doc::validate` scans again.

**Materialization-before-rejection:** yes for attribute strings/lists/maps, mark attrs, inline text (JSON `Box<str>` → `String` → split chunks), run counts, and node counts. Only JSON depth is rejected before subtree allocation.

### 2. Duplicate validation inside `from_json`

`decode_doc` calls `check_doc` (`parser.rs:86`), which calls `Doc::validate` (`parser.rs:105-115`); `from_fragment_json` does the same (`fragment.rs:61`).

Already checked during decode and re-checked by `Doc::validate`:
- attribute declaration membership + type + required + unsafe URL: `decode_attrs:64,75-91,97-104` vs `validate.rs:110-112` (`Schema::validate_attrs`) and `validate_marks` (URL at `validate.rs:~270-285`).
- `content_allows`: `parser.rs:187,207` vs `validate.rs:124,166`.
- node/kind resolution: `parser.rs:129-150` vs `validate.rs:105-108`.
- mutual exclusivity / mark-allowed: only in `validate_marks` (`validate.rs:246+`), not duplicated (gap, not duplication).

`Doc::new`'s limit scan is *not* duplicated by `validate`, but it is a third full traversal. `decode_attrs`/`decode_marks` have **no access** to limit constants: signatures are `decode_attrs(Option<&JsonValue>, &[AttrSpec], DecodePath)` (`attrs.rs:47-51`) and `decode_marks(Option<&JsonValue>, &Schema)` (`attrs.rs:231-234`).

`Doc::validate` itself allocates on the hot path: `kind_names` Vec per doc (`validate.rs:49-53`), kinds Vec per container (`:164-165`), `BTreeSet<NodeId>` (`:48`, insert `:114`), `MarkSet::clone()` per run (`:145`), `DocPath` per issue.

### 3. `JsonValue` / `check_json` vs decode

- `JsonValue` = `{ kind: JsonKind, start: u32 }` (`json.rs:10-14`). No end offsets/spans; strings are owned `Box<str>`, objects `Box<[(Box<str>, JsonValue)]>`, arrays `Box<[JsonValue]>`.
- **No zero-copy view path.** `Parser::string` copies input text (`json_parser.rs:170`) and `string_escaped` builds a fresh `String`; keys are likewise copied. Decode copies again.
- `check_json` (`parser.rs:38-40`) = `parse_json` only: syntax, trailing data, duplicate keys, floats/exponents, integer range, UTF-8/escapes, and `max_depth`. It ignores every other limit, schema, URL safety, and structure.
- Decode (`decode_doc`/`decode_block`/`decode_attrs`/`decode_marks`) does schema resolution, inline-vs-block decision, attrs/mark typing, unsafe-URL rejection, run normalization, then `Doc::new` limits, then `Doc::validate`.

### 4. Fuzz targets today

- `json_parse.rs`: `from_json` → `a11y_tree` → `to_json_string` → `validate_a11y` (guarded by `Ok`).
- `a11y_tree.rs`: identical logic to `json_parse.rs` (uses `let _ =` instead of binding). Redundant coverage.
- `apply_step.rs`: `from_json` → `EditorState::from_doc` → delete range → insert `"fuzz"` → `apply`.
- Missing targets: decode-only comparisons, **canonical round-trip** (`from_json` → `to_json_string` → `from_json`, byte equality), fragment/envelope round-trip, limit-focused (tiny `Limits`), and a parse-only (`check_json`) target.

### 5. Concrete low-risk changes

**A. Thread limits into decoding (enables all early rejects).**
- `wire/attrs.rs:47` `decode_attrs(..., limits: &crate::Limits)`; call sites `parser.rs:65,150,268`.
- `wire/attrs.rs:231` `decode_marks(..., limits: &crate::Limits)`; call site `parser.rs:255`.
- `parser.rs:233` `decode_inline(..., limits)`.

**B. Attr count/string limits before materialization.**
- In `decode_attrs`, immediately after extracting `members` (`attrs.rs:55-61`), before line 62:
  check `members.len() > usize::from(limits.max_attrs_per_node)` → `ParseError` (existing `limit` code, offset `value.start()`, `path.boxed()`).
- In `decode_value` (`attrs.rs:113`): add `limits` + `depth`; before `Box::from(text)` (`:115-118`), before `text.clone()` (`:208`), before `name.clone()` (`:144,:223`), and before collecting List/Map, check `text.len() > limits.max_attr_string_bytes` and `depth > limits.max_depth` (`AttrType::List/Map/Any` arms at `:128-148,:204-229`). Fill `offset` from `value.start()`.
- `decode_ref` (`:152-202`): check `doc`/`node`/`version` raw string lengths against `max_attr_string_bytes` before `DocId::new`/`NodeId::new`/`VersionTag::new`.

**C. Mark limits and O(k²) removal.**
- In `decode_marks` after `as_array` (`:236-247`): reject `values.len() > u64::BITS` (or a new `Limits::max_marks_per_run`) before the loop.
- Before `Attrs::new(decoded)` (`:273`): reject `decoded.len() > usize::from(limits.max_mark_attrs)`.
- Replace repeated `marks.with_mark(...)` (`:275`) with collecting `Vec<Mark>`/`Vec<MarkAttr>` and one sorted construction; add a crate-internal `MarkSet::from_marks` in `model/marks.rs` (near `with_mark`, `:105-131`) computing the mask in one pass. This removes k intermediate Vec clones.

**D. Inline text/run limits before construction.**
- In `decode_inline` (`parser.rs:249-256`): check `text.len() > limits.max_block_text_bytes` before `String::from(text)`.
- In `decode_block` inline branch (`parser.rs:209-215`): accumulate text bytes while decoding children and fail once the sum exceeds `limits.max_block_text_bytes`, before `TextBlock::new`.
- Check run count after `TextBlock::new` (post-merge) and before `normalize`: `items().len() > max_runs_per_block`; this preserves merge semantics better than checking raw `children.len()`. However, to reject before building, an early bound `children.len() > max_runs_per_block` is only conservative when marks differ; safest low-risk is to add an `InlineItem` count check inside `TextBlock::push` returning `Result` or a pre-pass count of runs with differing adjacent marks (no allocation).
- Fix `parser.rs:215`: pass `min(MAX_RUN_BYTES, max_block_text_bytes)` (cast to u32) rather than `max_block_text_bytes`. Today the default 1 MiB ceiling allows runs > `model::MAX_RUN_BYTES` (4096), which `validate.rs:136-138` then reports as `I4` after the fact.

**E. Node-count during decode.**
- Thread `&mut u32` (or `&mut DecodeBudget`) through `decode_blocks` (`parser.rs:88`) and `decode_block` (`:118`); increment per block/atom and reject `> limits.max_nodes` before pushing `Arc::new` (`:99,:221-229`). This makes `Doc::new`'s `count_descendants` (`doc.rs:103`) redundant for the decode path.

**F. Remove duplicate validation.**
- Add a crate-internal constructor `Doc::from_decoded(attrs, blocks)` (next to `Doc::new`, `doc.rs:82`) that only wraps `Chunks::new` without the depth/`check_block_limits`/`count_descendants` scan. Use it in `decode_doc` (`parser.rs:79`) and `fragment.rs:56` **after** decode-side limit enforcement (B–E) is in place. `Doc::new` remains the public checked constructor for programmatic builds.
- Drop `content_allows` from `decode_block` (`parser.rs:187,207`): decide inline vs container solely by `child_spec.inline` (`:184-187,203-207`); `Doc::validate` reports `I2` at `validate.rs:124,166` as before. This removes one content-machine run per container.
- Reduce `Doc::validate` allocations: replace `previous = Some(run.marks.clone())` (`validate.rs:145`) with an index into `text.items()` (compare against the prior text run); replace `kind_names` (`:49-53`) and child `kinds` (`:164-165`) only if a streaming `ContentMachine::allows` API is added (higher risk; optional).
- Keep `Doc::validate` public and complete; do not weaken it.
- `check_doc` calls remain necessary for structural invariants only (I1–I12) not covered by decode (mark excludes, empty container, size arithmetic, tables).

**G. Test files to extend.**
- `tests/parser_limits.rs`: add cases for `max_attrs_per_node`, `max_mark_attrs`, `max_nodes`, `max_depth` nested attrs, and assert rejection occurs with the small limit *and* a stable error code (currently only text/run/attr-string are covered at `:74-121`).
- `tests/parser_validation.rs`: add canonical round-trip for attribute lists/maps and a >4096-byte run (currently would be rejected with `I4`).
- New/expanded `tests/alloc.rs` or `tests/memory.rs`: assert `from_json` allocation count/peak for a rejected oversized attr string does not scale with input size (would fail today). These use unsafe global allocator wrappers, allowed today by `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` in tests but note repo rule “no unwrap/expect/panic in tests” — use the existing `let Ok(...) else { return; }` style.
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/`: add `round_trip.rs` (`from_json` → `to_json_string` → `from_json` byte equality, valid docs only) and a `limits.rs` target with tiny `Limits`; merge `json_parse.rs`/`a11y_tree.rs` (identical) or differentiate them.
- `bench/benches/hot_path.rs:75-85`: optionally add `from_json` with a rejected oversized attr to measure early rejection; `check_json` benchmark already exists at `:93-97`.

### 6. Golden / byte-stable tests constraining encoder–decoder

- `tests/smoke.rs:39-49` — exact canonical document string (UTF-8 and mark ordering); `:64-67` a11y JSON substrings.
- `tests/editing.rs:40-43` — exact JSON after insertion; `:168-183` undo byte-equality.
- `tests/fragment_json.rs:35,51,63` — exact fragment bytes and round-trip stability.
- `tests/schema_full_attrs.rs:108-121` — canonical sorted map keys (`"metadata":{"a":"1","b":"2"}`) and round-trip equality.
- `tests/parser_validation.rs:60-70` — strong-link mark canonical round-trip.
- `tests/doc_view.rs:36-58` — exact view JSON substrings/ranges (projection only, not canonical doc).
- `tests/alloc.rs:100-113,152-163` and `tests/memory.rs:97-121` — allocation/byte budgets (hot path and document build), not wire bytes, but any new per-node allocation on decode must not regress these if reused.
- `bench/benches/hot_path.rs:47-72` — builds 10k-block docs then serializes; run splitting/limit changes must not make `document()` fail (100-byte runs, well below `MAX_RUN_BYTES`).

All decoder changes must keep accepting exactly the canonical forms above; run splitting at `MAX_RUN_BYTES` does not affect these fixtures (all runs < 4096 bytes).

### Critical Files for Implementation
- `crates/rich-editor-auy/src/wire/attrs.rs` — add limits parameters and pre-materialization checks in `decode_attrs`/`decode_value`/`decode_marks`.
- `crates/rich-editor-auy/src/wire/parser.rs` — thread node budget, early text/run checks, fix `normalize` ceiling, drop duplicate `content_allows`.
- `crates/rich-editor-auy/src/model/doc.rs` — add `from_decoded` unchecked constructor to avoid the redundant whole-tree limit scan.
- `crates/rich-editor-auy/src/model/marks.rs` — add one-pass `MarkSet::from_marks` to remove O(k²) clones.
- `crates/rich-editor-auy/tests/parser_limits.rs` — extend coverage for attr/mark/node limits and early rejection.
